newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-GRAF HOPEFUL OF PLAYING IN TOKYO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF HOPEFUL OF PLAYING IN TOKYO.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf, who has been suffering from a fever since her shock fourth round exit at the Australian Open, said on Wednesday she still hoped to play the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo next week.
South Africa's Amanda Coetzer ended Graf's record 45-match unbeaten run in grand slam tournaments on Sunday with a straight sets victory on a scorching day at Melbourne Park.
Graf, whose father Peter's trial on tax evasion charges is expected to reach a verdict on January 24, left the stadium immediately after the match suffering heat exhaustion.
"The doctor said that I can try to hit a few balls when I'm finished with the antibiotics, so hopefully I can try on Friday on Saturday," Graf said in a statement.
The German added she was "definitely wanting to play" the tournament in Tokyo starting on Tuesday.
Graf has kept largely to her Melbourne hotel, recuperating after receiving treatment for an infected toe and fever.
"I've been staying in, pretty much letting myself recover," she said. "The doctor's orders were to rest and that's what I've been doing.
"I've had a fever that we thought was due to the toe, but they think now that it may not have been related. I just may have picked up a virus somewhere."
Graf's Australian Open defeat was her worst result in Melbourne since losing in the third round as a 14-year-old in 1984.
Her extraordinary grand slam record in the professional era dated back to her defeat at the final of the U.S. Open in 1994 when she lost to Spain's Arantxa Sanchez Vicario.

The German, who had long bettered Margaret Smith Court's record of winning 35 consecutive grand slam matches, wilted on Sunday in heat said to be up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit) on the court.
